units.sourceHTML: 8.1 Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate

units.text: You can select all unmerged changes from ⟦0⟧ to ⟦1⟧ for merging into ⟦2⟧ with the ⟦3⟧ (⟦4⟧) option. You can select only the nonoverlapping unmerged changes with ⟦5⟧ (⟦6⟧), and you can select only the overlapping changes with ⟦7⟧ (⟦8⟧).
units.sourceHTML: You can select all unmerged changes from older to yours for merging into mine with the --ed (-e) option. You can select only the nonoverlapping unmerged changes with --easy-only (-3), and you can select only the overlapping changes with --overlap-only (-x).

units.text: The ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ options select only ⟦3⟧unmerged changes⟦4⟧, i.e. changes where ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ differ; they ignore changes from ⟦7⟧ to ⟦8⟧ where ⟦9⟧ and ⟦10⟧ are identical, because they assume that such changes have already been merged. If this assumption is not a safe one, you can use the ⟦11⟧ (⟦12⟧) option (see ⟦13⟧Marking Conflicts⟦14⟧).
units.sourceHTML: The -e, -3 and -x options select only unmerged changes, i.e. changes where mine and yours differ; they ignore changes from older to yours where mine and yours are identical, because they assume that such changes have already been merged. If this assumption is not a safe one, you can use the --show-all (-A) option (see Marking Conflicts).

units.text: Here is the output of the command ⟦0⟧ with each of these three options (see ⟦1⟧A Third Sample Input File⟦2⟧, for the complete contents of the files). Notice that ⟦3⟧ outputs the union of the disjoint sets of changes output by ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧.
